spoken_text: He followed me to my car. So I barked. It was past eleven when I left the store. The parking structure was mostly empty — just the fluorescent hum and the sound of my own footsteps echoing up through the levels. I don't usually notice things. But I noticed him. He came in just after me and matched my pace exactly. When I slowed, he slowed. When I took the stairs instead of the elevator, he followed. By the time I reached Level Three, my keys were already between my fingers. But instead of running, I stopped. Turned around. And started barking. Full volume. Five full seconds. He froze. Then he looked around — like he expected a dog to appear from somewhere. Then he backed toward the elevator without a single word. Just that strange silence you get when something doesn't go the way someone planned. I drove home shaking but intact. I've thought about that moment a hundred times since. I don't know if he meant harm. But the barking stopped the approach — and sometimes that's enough. Follow if you carry your keys like that. Stay aware out there.
title: He Followed Me Through the Garage — So I Barked
